messages:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: embeddings.prod.routed QPS spike to ~12k (baseline ~200) + 5xx ~8%. Possible credentialed scraper or fanout abuse. Paging @oncall-sre @eng-ml.
Maya (SRE): I'm up — joining. Any quick triage pointers?
Sanjay (Eng-Infra): pulling top callers now. Initial K/V: one API key shows extreme parallelism, same small set of user agents. Looks like small fanout from multiple cloud IPs.
Lee (Support): Any customer-facing errors so far? Which endpoints?
Oncall Bot: Affected endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings/batch and /v1/embeddings (single) — batch has highest QPS.
Maya (SRE): Can we do an immediate soft-throttle on batch while we investigate? Prefer rate-slice by API-key first, then region if needed.
Sanjay (Eng-Infra): I have a fast patch to add per-key dynamic caps. Pushing now. Patch snippet: ```bash
curl -X PATCH https://config.internal/api/rate-limits
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"selector":"api_key:K_*","limit_per_min":3000}'
```
Oncall Bot: Deploy started to edge config in 2s, rollout 20% -> 100% over ~1m.
Maya (SRE): Also enabling temporary WAF rule to block UA fingerprint "curl/7" variants and a handful of obvious bot UAs. Doing that now.
Infra Runbook Bot: Runbook check: for high-volume embeddings abuse, recommended mitigations: per-key throttles, disable batch endpoint, WAF UA block, geo-rate-slice.
Olivia (Product): Please avoid full-service shutdown unless unavoidable — prefer targeted mitigations. Notify customers proactively if they see 429s.
Sanjay (Eng-Infra): Quick update: applied per-key cap for the top offending key; QPS for that key dropped from ~9k to ~700 immediately. Overall QPS down to ~3.2k.
Maya (SRE): Still seeing >2k QPS coming from a set of IPs in Southeast Asia — enabling geo-based rate-slice for APAC low-tier (VN/ID/PH) to 20% throttle.
Lee (Support): I'm drafting a short notice for customers hitting 429/503: "We're experiencing elevated automated traffic on embeddings; we've applied throttles to protect availability. If you see errors please reach out and include request id." Will post to status and CS inbox.
Maya (SRE): Next step: disable batch embeddings as it's easiest vector for fanout. Toggle: `rb flags set embeddings.batch.enabled false`. Executing.
Sanjay (Eng-Infra): Applied feature-toggle. Batch endpoint now returns 429 with structured error: `{"code":"rate_limited","message":"batch embeddings temporarily restricted"}`.
Olivia (Product): Good. Can we fallback single-row embeddings with stricter per-request limits so paying customers can degrade gracefully?
Maya (SRE): Yes — we kept single-row path open with limit 10rps/key. Monitoring impact.
Oncall Bot: Metrics update: total QPS down from 12k -> 1.2k after combined changes. 5xx dropped to ~1.5%.
Lee (Support): Two customers (acct: acme-corp, acct: fluxai) reported elevated 429s. Sent targeted note and collected logs. No SLA breach detected yet but will keep monitoring.
Sanjay (Eng-Infra): Added WAF block for UA regex and a small ASN block for the worst offenders. Also applied short-lived IP rate-limit at edge for 60s token bucket.
Maya (SRE): I'm going to run a deeper query to see if keys were leaked vs credential stuffing. Query: ```sql
SELECT src_ip, api_key, count(*) as calls
FROM ingress_logs
WHERE path LIKE '/v1/embeddings%'
AND ts > now()-interval '30 minutes'
GROUP BY src_ip, api_key
ORDER BY calls DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
Maya (SRE): Early result: same api_key used across many src_ips in <1hr window — likely credential stuffing or recycled key.
Olivia (Product): Which customers mapped to that key? Any enterprise keys?
Sanjay (Eng-Infra): The key is associated with a dev sandbox, not an enterprise paid key. Noting rate-limits are safe.
Lee (Support): I'll reach out to the sandbox account owner to recommend key rotation. Also putting a suggested KB article for customers on key rotation.
Maya (SRE): Operational checklist: 1) Keep per-key caps for 6h 2) Keep batch disabled for now 3) Keep UA WAF rule 4) Re-evaluate geo throttle in 30m.
Olivia (Product): Assign a postmortem owner — I'll take P0 for customer comms and playbook updates.
Maya (SRE): I'll own the technical postmortem and mitigations doc.
Oncall Bot: Handoff: Maya is primary for the next shift. @Lee will act as comms lead. Scheduled follow-up call in 30m.
Maya (SRE): Quick note for SRE oncall in handoff: if QPS creeps back above 2k, re-enable stricter ASN blocks and escalate to infra for temporary key revocation.
Lee (Support): Logged incident in PagerDuty, noted impacted customers and actions taken. Drafted status update to go out in 15m.
Sanjay (Eng-Infra): Leaving a small rollout of a more aggressive per-IP SYN flood protection at the edge for the next hour; rollback planned if false positives.
Maya (SRE): Final metrics snapshot before handoff: QPS 1.1k, 5xx 1.1%, error type majority 429 (rate_limited). Customer visible impact limited to sandbox/dev and a couple of paid customers with transient 429s; CS has tickets.
Olivia (Product): Post-incident actions: (a) add automated detection for high per-key fanout, (b) make batch-disable fallback more graceful with header guidance, (c) add a playbook step to rotate keys for suspected credential-stuffing.
Maya (SRE): Acknowledged. Adding tasks to incidents board and will attach logs. Handoff complete — I'm going offline in 10m, Lee will continue monitoring.
Oncall Bot: :white_check_mark: Handed off. Please add any follow-up notes to the incident thread.
